pageTitle: Functions & Basic Error Handling - Python Theory

header.title: Functions & Basic Error Handling
header.subtitle: Foundation Level • 50 minutes • Create reusable code and handle errors gracefully

introduction.title: Introduction to Functions
introduction.paragraph1: Functions are reusable blocks of code that perform specific tasks. They help organize code, reduce repetition, and make programs more modular and maintainable.
introduction.callout: What you'll learn: How to define and call functions, work with parameters and return values, understand variable scope, and handle errors gracefully with try-except blocks.

reusability.title: Code Reusability
reusability.description: Write once, use many times. Functions eliminate code duplication.

organization.title: Organization
organization.description: Break complex problems into smaller, manageable pieces.

testing.title: Testing
testing.description: Functions can be tested independently, making debugging easier.

collaboration.title: Collaboration
collaboration.description: Team members can work on different functions simultaneously.

definingFunctions.title: Defining Functions
definingFunctions.paragraph1: Functions are defined using the def keyword followed by the function name, parentheses, and a colon. The function body is indented.
namingRules: Start with a letter or underscore
bestPractices: Keep functions focused on one task
tips: The def keyword defines the function but doesn't execute it
Functions must be defined before they are called
Functions can be defined inside other functions

parametersArguments.title: Parameters & Arguments
parametersArguments.paragraph1: Parameters are variables in function definitions. Arguments are the actual values passed to functions when called.
parametersArguments.requiredDescription: Must be provided when calling the function
parametersArguments.defaultDescription: Have default values if not provided

returnValues.title: Return Values
returnValues.paragraph1: The return statement sends a value back to the function caller. Functions without explicit return statements return None.
bestPractices: Always return the same data type when possible
Use early returns to simplify logic
importantNotes: Multiple return values are returned as a tuple

scope.title: Variable Scope
scope.paragraph1: Scope determines where variables can be accessed in your code. Python has local, global, and built-in scopes.
scope.legbParagraph: Python follows the LEGB rule for variable lookup:
bestPractices: Pass values as parameters instead of using globals
Keep variable scope as narrow as possible

errorHandling.title: Basic Error Handling
errorHandling.paragraph1: Error handling allows your programs to gracefully handle unexpected situations without crashing. Use try-except blocks to catch and handle exceptions.

practice.title: Practice Exercises
practice.exercise1Description: Create functions for basic arithmetic operations with error handling.
practice.exercise2Description: Build a function that calculates and returns letter grades.
practice.exercise3Description: Create a function that safely gets and validates user input.
practice.exercise4Description: Build functions to process and analyze a list of numbers.
practice.ctaDescription: Take our interactive quiz to see how well you've mastered functions and error handling!
